item.title: Writing a Scanner
item.description: Build a scanner that turns source text into a stream of numbers, operators, and other tokens while handling whitespace, unknown input, and end of file.

item.title: x86_64 Instruction Encoding Overview
item.description: An overview of how x86_64 instruction encoding works across legacy, VEX, and EVEX encoding families, followed by a manual encoding walkthrough for one form of the MOV instruction.

item.title: Building a Scanner
item.description: Start the Fyn compiler in Go by defining source files and tokens, then scanning keywords, identifiers, integers, punctuation, and source locations.

item.title: Writing a TDOP/Pratt Parser
item.description: Turn tokens into an abstract syntax tree with a Pratt parser, using binding powers to correctly handle operator precedence and associativity.

item.title: Encoding SYSCALL and RET with NASM Listing Tests
item.description:
Setting up the first version of the encoder and a NASM listing-based test harness, using simple zero-operand instructions to verify that generated bytes match known assembler output.

Instructions covered: SYSCALL and RET.

item.title: Building a Pratt Parser
item.description: Build a precedence-aware Pratt parser that turns Fyn expressions into an AST while supporting prefix, infix, and postfix operators with configurable associativity.

item.title: Writing a Tree-Walk Interpreter
item.description: Create a tree-walk interpreter that recursively evaluates the abstract syntax tree and computes arithmetic results.

item.title: Encoding Register Operands with ModRM and MOV
item.description:
Implementing register-to-register instruction encoding using ModRM bytes, register operands, width selection, opcode emission, and REX prefix generation.

Instructions and forms covered include register/register MOV-style encodings and the ModRM.mod=11 register operand form.

item.title: Building Parser Test Infrastructure
item.description: Create readable AST snapshots and source-embedded parser fixtures using trivia, node spans, tree walking, and automated expected-output comparisons.

item.title: Adding Unary Prefix Operators
item.description: Extend the parser and interpreter with unary prefix operators, including correctly binding and evaluating unary minus and plus.

item.title: Encoding Memory Operands with ModRM and MOV
item.description:
Extending the encoder from register operands to memory operands using ModRM addressing forms, including base-register memory accesses and the special cases for stack and base-pointer registers.

Instructions and addressing cases covered include memory/register MOV-style forms, SP/R12 addressing, and BP/R13 displacement handling.

item.title: Parsing Functions and Improving Parser Errors
item.description: Strengthen parser tests and diagnostics, then add module, function-declaration, and block nodes with error recovery and AST support.

item.title: Adding Unary Postfix Operators
item.description: Add factorial as a unary postfix operator, covering its precedence, AST representation, evaluation, and edge cases.

item.title: Encoding SIB Addressing and Displacements with MOV
item.description:
Adding SIB byte support for scaled-index addressing, displacement encoding, no-base addressing, and canonicalization of some addressing forms.

Addressing cases covered include base + displacement, base + index * scale, no-base SIB forms, SP/R12 SIB requirements, and BP/R13 displacement requirements.

item.title: Building a Type Checker
item.description: Parse function return types and return statements, then build an interned type system and annotate expression nodes with checked types.

item.title: Changing Order of Operations with Groups
item.description: Add parenthesised groups so programs can explicitly override normal operator precedence while preserving groups in the AST.

item.title: Encoding RIP-Relative and Explicit Displacements with MOV
item.description: Adding RIP-relative addressing and improving displacement handling so the encoder can skip zero displacements.

item.title: Type-Checking Return Statements
item.description: Add function types and lexical environments, resolve built-in type names, and validate return counts and expression types inside functions.

item.title: Parsing Expression Statements
item.description: Move beyond standalone expressions by parsing semicolon-terminated expression statements into a program that the interpreter can execute.

item.title: Matching Instruction Forms with MOV
item.description:
Introducing instruction form metadata so the encoder can choose the correct encoding form based on operation, operand widths, and operand kinds.

Instructions and concepts covered include MOV register/memory forms, form matching, opcode map selection, ModRM/no-ModRM handling, and using matched forms to drive byte emission.

item.title: Generating Basic IR
item.description: Design a linear intermediate representation and recursively lower typed Fyn functions, constants, returns, and binary expressions into readable IR.

item.title: Adding Return Statements
item.description: Introduce keywords, identifiers, and return statements, including optional return values and early termination of program execution.

item.title: Encoding MOV Immediates, +r, and /digit Forms
item.description:
Adding immediate operands, immediate-width selection, MOV immediate forms, opcode +r encodings, opcode-extension /digit encodings, and form scoring for shorter instruction encodings.

Instructions and forms covered include MOV immediate-to-register, MOV immediate-to-r/m, imm8/imm16/imm32/imm64 emission, +r opcode forms, /digit opcode-extension forms, and SIB transform fixes.

item.title: Intel SDM, Vol 1, Basic Execution Environment and Procedures
item.description: Study the Intel Software Developer's Manual to understand notation, operating modes, registers, memory addressing, procedures, and core integer instructions before writing the backend.

item.title: Executing Functions
item.description: Parse function declarations and blocks, then execute a main function using nested environments for name lookup and lexical scope.

item.title: Encoding Op/En Metadata for MOV Forms
item.description:
Replacing operand-role guessing with explicit Op/En metadata, so each instruction form can describe which operand is encoded in ModRM.reg, ModRM.r/m, immediates, opcode bits, or fixed implicit locations.

Encoding concepts covered include Intel Op/En notation, MR/RM/OI/MI-style forms, operand role selection, and mapping instruction forms to encoder behavior.

item.title: Intel SDM Vol 2, Instruction Format and Encoding
item.description: Read Intel's instruction-format reference to learn prefixes, opcodes, ModR/M, SIB, REX, displacements, immediates, and the notation used by instruction tables.

item.title: Variables, Block Statements, and Nested Block Returns
item.description: Add variable declarations, identifier expressions, and explicit blocks, then use stack unwinding to support returns from deeply nested scopes.

item.title: Encoding ADD/SUB, MUL/DIV, and IMUL/IDIV
item.description:
Implementing the core integer arithmetic instructions and the form metadata needed for register, memory, immediate, accumulator, and implicit-register encodings.

Instructions covered: ADD, SUB, MUL, DIV, IMUL, and IDIV.

item.title: Encoding Register-to-Register MOV
item.description: Start the x86-64 encoder with register operands and implement tested register-to-register MOV encoding using operand-size, ModR/M, and REX fields.

item.title: Parsing and Executing Function Calls
item.description: Parse and execute function-call expressions while resolving the interaction between call, unary, and binary operator precedence.

item.title: Encoding AND/OR/XOR, TEST, NOT, and NEG
item.description:
Adding bitwise logical instructions, test instructions, and unary arithmetic forms, reusing the same ModRM, immediate, and opcode-extension machinery from the arithmetic encoder.

Instructions covered: AND, OR, XOR, TEST, NOT, and NEG.

item.title: Encoding Register/Memory MOV
item.description: Extend MOV encoding to register-to-memory and memory-to-register operations, including the special RSP/R12 SIB and RBP/R13 displacement forms.

item.title: Encoding SAL/SHL/SHR/SAR and RCL/RCR/ROL/ROR
item.description:
Implementing shift and rotate instructions, including immediate-count forms, CL-count forms, and single-bit implicit-count forms.

Instructions covered: SAL, SAR, SHL, SHR, RCL, RCR, ROL, and ROR.

item.title: Encoding Memory Displacements
item.description: Encode base-plus-displacement and RIP-relative MOV operands while selecting compact disp8 forms and handling base-pointer exceptions.

item.title: Encoding CMP, CMOVcc, and SETcc
item.description:
Adding compare instructions and condition-code based result instructions, including aliases for equivalent x86 condition mnemonics.

Instructions covered: CMP, CMOVcc, SETcc, and aliases such as CMOVZ/CMOVE, CMOVC/CMOVB, SETZ/SETE, and SETC/SETB.

item.title: Encoding Scaled-Index Addressing
item.description: Implement SIB encoding for scaled-index effective addresses, including scale conversion, REX extensions, missing-base forms, and special stack/base registers.

item.title: Encoding PUSH/POP, JMP/Jcc, and CALL
item.description:
Implementing stack operations, relative branches, conditional jumps, and calls, including displacement width selection and relative-offset encoding.

Instructions covered: PUSH, POP, JMP, Jcc, and CALL.

item.title: Encoding Immediate MOV
item.description: Add immediate-source MOV forms for register and memory destinations using opcode-register extensions, /digit fields, REX rules, and width-aware immediates.

item.title: Encoding LEA, MOVSX/MOVSXD/MOVZX, and CBW-CQO
item.description:
Adding address calculation and integer sign/zero-extension instructions, including operand-local source widths and forms that force REX.W.

Instructions covered: LEA, MOVSX, MOVSXD, MOVZX, CBW, CWDE, CDQE, CWD, CDQ, and CQO.

item.title: Improving x86-64 Encoder Tests
item.description: Add encoder assertions and replace repetitive hand-written cases with a compact instruction parser that derives operands, sizes, registers, immediates, and memory addresses.

item.title: Encoding BSF/BSR, BT/BTC/BTR/BTS, LZCNT/TZCNT, and POPCNT
item.description:
Implementing bit scan, bit test, and bit count instructions, including mandatory prefixes and register/memory bit-operation forms.

Instructions covered: BSF, BSR, BT, BTC, BTR, BTS, LZCNT, TZCNT, and POPCNT.

item.title: Encoding LEA, ADD, and SUB
item.description: Grow the encoder beyond MOV by implementing LEA and shared ADD/SUB forms for registers, memory, immediates, and accumulator-specific opcodes.

item.title: Encoding POP r/m, JECXZ/JRCXZ, CPUID/RDTSC, NOP, and XCHG
item.description:
Filling in several scalar instruction gaps while improving the encoder test cases, explicit displacement helpers, and form matching behavior.

Instructions covered: POP r/m, JECXZ, JRCXZ, CPUID, RDTSC, NOP, and XCHG.

item.title: Encoding MUL, DIV, and RET
item.description: Complete the initial instruction set with sign-extended ADD/SUB immediates, implicit-register MUL/DIV forms, and the single-byte RET instruction.

item.title: Encoding Legacy SSE/VEX/EVEX Prefixes with MOVAPS and VMOVAP
item.description:
Using MOVAPS as the first vector instruction to introduce SSE register operands, legacy SSE encoding, VEX prefix encoding, EVEX prefix encoding, and the rules for choosing between VEX and EVEX forms.

Instructions and forms covered: MOVAPS and VMOVAPS across legacy SSE, VEX, and EVEX encodings.

item.title: Lowering IR to x86-64 Machine Code
item.description: Connect the IR and x86-64 encoder with naive virtual-register allocation, operand conversion, instruction dispatch, and end-to-end disassembly.

item.title: Encoding EVEX Masks with MOVAPS/PD, VMOVAPS/PD, MOVUPS/PD, and VMOVUPS/PD
item.description:
Adding EVEX opmask and zeroing-mask support, then extending the vector move implementation across aligned and unaligned single/double-precision move instructions.

Instructions covered: MOVAPS, VMOVAPS, MOVAPD, VMOVAPD, MOVUPS, VMOVUPS, MOVUPD, and VMOVUPD, including EVEX {k} and {z} decorators.

item.title: Writing PE32+ Executables
item.description: Write a PE32+ image generator from the Windows specification, emit headers and sections, inspect the binary, and run generated x86-64 code as a native executable.

item.title: Encoding MOVSS/SD, VMOVSS/SD, MOVDQA/U, and VMOVDQA/U/8/16/32/64
item.description:
Expanding vector move support to scalar floating-point moves and integer vector moves, including stricter form matching, 3-operand VEX/EVEX forms, and decorator-aware form scoring.

Instructions covered: MOVSS, MOVSD, VMOVSS, VMOVSD, MOVDQA, VMOVDQA, VMOVDQA32, VMOVDQA64, MOVDQU, VMOVDQU, VMOVDQU8, VMOVDQU16, VMOVDQU32, and VMOVDQU64.

item.title: Encoding EVEX Rounding/Broadcasts with ADD/VADD, VSUB, VMUL, and VDIV SS/SD/PS/PD
item.description:
Adding scalar and packed floating-point arithmetic instructions, then extending EVEX encoding to support embedded rounding, rounding-control values, and memory broadcast operands.

Instructions covered: ADDSS, ADDSD, ADDPS, ADDPD, VADDSS, VADDSD, VADDPS, VADDPD, VSUBSS, VSUBSD, VSUBPS, VSUBPD, VMULSS, VMULSD, VMULPS, VMULPD, VDIVSS, VDIVSD, VDIVPS, and VDIVPD.

item.title: Encoding EVEX Compressed Disp8 and Tuple Types
item.description:
Implementing EVEX compressed disp8 encoding, where an 8-bit displacement is scaled by the instruction tuple type instead of representing a raw byte offset.

Encoding concepts covered include EVEX compressed disp8, tuple types, full-vector memory tuples, broadcast tuples, scalar tuples, displacement scaling, and fallback to disp32.

item.title: Encoding SAE with COMISS/SD, UCOMISS/SD, and SHUF/VSHUF PS/PD
item.description:
Adding SAE handling and implementing scalar floating-point compare instructions plus immediate-controlled shuffle instructions for packed floating-point vectors.

Instructions covered: COMISS, VCOMISS, COMISD, VCOMISD, UCOMISS, VUCOMISS, UCOMISD, VUCOMISD, SHUFPS, VSHUFPS, SHUFPD, and VSHUFPD.

item.title: Encoding GPR/XMM Transfers with MOVD/Q and VMOVD/Q
item.description:
Adding MOVD, MOVQ, VMOVD, and VMOVQ to the x86-64 encoder, covering transfers between general-purpose registers, memory operands, and XMM/vector registers.

This video covers legacy SSE forms, VEX forms, VEX.W encoding, short MOVQ encodings, and the distinction between 32-bit MOVD transfers and 64-bit MOVQ transfers.

Instructions covered: MOVD, MOVQ, VMOVD, and VMOVQ.

item.title: Encoding CVT/VCVT and CVTT/VCVTT Scalar SS/SD Conversions
item.description:
Adding scalar x86-64 conversion instructions for moving between floating-point values and signed integers, including both rounded CVT forms and truncating CVTT forms.

This video covers scalar single-precision and double-precision conversion forms, VEX-encoded conversion forms, register and memory operands, 32-bit and 64-bit integer operands, and allowing SAE/ER decorators on register operands where the encoding permits it.

Instructions covered: CVTSS2SI, VCVTSS2SI, CVTSD2SI, VCVTSD2SI, CVTTSS2SI, VCVTTSS2SI, CVTTSD2SI, VCVTTSD2SI, CVTSS2SD, VCVTSS2SD, CVTSD2SS, VCVTSD2SS, CVTSI2SS, VCVTSI2SS, CVTSI2SD, and VCVTSI2SD.

item.title: Encoding CVT/VCVT and CVTT/VCVTT Packed PS/PD/DQ Conversions
item.description:
Adding packed floating-point and integer conversion instructions, including legacy SSE, VEX, and EVEX forms. This covers packed single/double precision conversions, signed doubleword integer conversions, truncating CVTT variants, EVEX SAE handling, and form fixes needed for scalar and packed conversion instructions.

Instructions covered: CVTPS2DQ, VCVTPS2DQ, CVTTPS2DQ, VCVTTPS2DQ, CVTDQ2PS, VCVTDQ2PS, CVTPD2DQ, VCVTPD2DQ, CVTTPD2DQ, VCVTTPD2DQ, CVTDQ2PD, VCVTDQ2PD, CVTPS2PD, VCVTPS2PD, CVTPD2PS, and VCVTPD2PS.

item.title: Encoding CMP/VCMP SS/SD/PS/PD and PCMPEQ/PCMPGT B/W/D/Q
item.description:
Adding scalar and packed floating-point comparison instructions with immediate comparison predicates, followed by packed integer equality and signed greater-than comparisons across byte, word, doubleword, and quadword element sizes.

Instructions covered: CMPSS, VCMPSS, CMPSD, VCMPSD, CMPPS, VCMPPS, CMPPD, VCMPPD, PCMPEQB, VPCMPEQB, PCMPEQW, VPCMPEQW, PCMPEQD, VPCMPEQD, PCMPEQQ, VPCMPEQQ, PCMPGTB, VPCMPGTB, PCMPGTW, VPCMPGTW, PCMPGTD, VPCMPGTD, PCMPGTQ, and VPCMPGTQ.

item.title: Encoding LOCK/REP Prefixes and CS/SS/DS/ES/FS/GS Segments
item.description:
Adding standalone instruction prefix forms for LOCK, REP, REPE/REPZ, and REPNE/REPNZ, then implementing segment override prefixes as memory operand decorators for CS, SS, DS, ES, FS, and GS.

Instructions covered: LOCK, REPNE, REPNZ, REP, REPE, REPZ, and CS, SS, DS, ES, FS, and GS segment override prefixes.

item.title: Encoding MOVS/CMPS/LODS/SCAS/STOS, CMPXCHG/XADD, Fences, and Cache Ops
item.description:
Implementing string instructions, atomic read-modify-write instructions, memory fences, pause, prefetch, and cache-line write-back/flush instructions.

Encoding cases covered include implicit string-operation operands, width-selected string opcodes, fixed ModRM encodings, atomic register/memory forms, memory-ordering instructions, prefetch locality variants, and cache-management instruction forms.

Instructions covered: MOVSB/W/D/Q, CMPSB/W/D/Q, LODSB/W/D/Q, SCASB/W/D/Q, STOSB/W/D/Q, CMPXCHG, XADD, L/S/MFENCE, PAUSE, PREFETCH T0/T1/T2/NTA/IT0/IT1, CLFLUSH, CLFLUSHOPT, and CLWB.

item.title: Encoding Flags, INT/UD, RDTSCP/XGETBV, RDRAND/SEED, IRET/SYSRET, and ENTER/LEAVE
item.description:
Implementing flag manipulation, trap/undefined-instruction, timestamp/control-register utility, random-number, system return, and stack-frame instructions.

Encoding cases covered include zero-operand flag instructions, stack flag save/restore forms, fixed trap opcodes, undefined-instruction encodings, system utility instructions with fixed operands, random-number register forms, SYSRET/IRET width handling, and ENTER/LEAVE stack-frame forms.

Instructions covered: CLC, CMC, STC, LAHF, SAHF, PUSHFQ, POPFQ, INT3, UD0, UD1, UD2, RDTSCP, XGETBV, XSETBV, RDRAND, RDSEED, SYSRET, IRETQ, ENTER, and LEAVE.

item.title: Encoding ADC/SBB, INC/DEC, SHLD/SHRD, BSWAP, MOVBE, and CRC32
item.description:
Adding more integer and utility instruction encodings to the x86_64 encoder, including carry-aware arithmetic, increment/decrement forms, double-precision shifts, byte-swap operations, endian-swapping memory moves, and CRC32 checksum instructions.

This covers a few encoding edge cases, including ENTER form fixes, renaming Op to Mnemonic, SHLD/SHRD operand forms, BSWAP +r encoding, MOVBE load/store forms, and CRC32 short-form selection for byte-source operands.

Instructions covered: ADC, SBB, INC, DEC, SHLD, SHRD, BSWAP, MOVBE, and CRC32.

item.title: Encoding ANDN, BEXTR, BZHI, MULX, PDEP/PEXT, RORX, SARX/SHLX/SHRX
item.description:
Adding BMI1 and BMI2 instruction encodings to the x86_64 encoder, covering VEX-encoded integer bit-manipulation forms, three-operand register/memory layouts, and immediate/control operand handling.

Instructions covered: ANDN, BEXTR, BZHI, MULX, PDEP, PEXT, RORX, SARX, SHLX, and SHRX.

item.title: Encoding AND/ANDN/OR/XOR PS/PD, MIN/MAX, SQRT, RCP, and RSQRT
item.description:
Adding a set of scalar and packed floating-point SIMD utility instructions to the x86_64 encoder, covering logical vector operations, min/max comparisons, square roots, reciprocals, and reciprocal square roots.

Instructions covered: ANDPS, ANDPD, ANDNPS, ANDNPD, ORPS, ORPD, XORPS, XORPD, MAXPS/PD/SS/SD, MINPS/PD/SS/SD, SQRTPS/PD/SS/SD, RCPPS, RCPSS, RSQRTPS, and RSQRTSS.

item.title: Generating Go Tests from NASM Comments
item.description:
Unifying the x86_64 encoder test cases by moving the Go-side test metadata into NASM comments, so each NASM instruction line also describes the corresponding encoder call.

This video adds a small test-generation step that reads structured comments from the NASM test file, parses mnemonic, width, and operand notation, and generates Go test cases from the same source used to assemble the expected bytes.

item.title: Encoding BLEND/VBLEND, PBLEND, DP, INSERTPS, and EXTRACTPS
item.description:
Adding blend, dot-product, insert, and extract instruction encodings to the x86_64 encoder, including immediate-controlled blend masks, variable blend mask registers, packed integer blend forms, dot-product control immediates, and scalar lane insertion/extraction.

Instructions covered: BLENDPS, BLENDPD, BLENDVPS, BLENDVPD, PBLENDW, PBLENDVB, DPPD, DPPS, INSERTPS, and EXTRACTPS.

item.title: Encoding LDDQU, MOVDUP, MOVHL/LHPS, MOVH/LPS/PD, MOVMSK, MOVNT, and VMASKMOV
item.description:
Adding SSE and AVX MOV variants for duplicating, rearranging, masking, and transferring packed data, along with non-temporal stores and masked vector memory operations.

Instructions covered: LDDQU/VLDDQU, MOVDDUP, MOVSHDUP, MOVSLDUP, MOVHLPS, MOVLHPS, MOVHPD, MOVHPS, MOVLPD, MOVLPS, MOVMSKPS, MOVMSKPD, MOVNTDQ/VMOVNTDQ, MOVNTI, MOVNTPD/VMOVNTPD, MOVNTPS/VMOVNTPS, and VMASKMOV.

item.title: Encoding AESENC/LAST, AESDEC/LAST, AESIMC, AESKEYGENASSIST, and PCLMULQDQ
item.description:
Adding AES round, inverse-round, key-generation, and inverse-mix-column instructions, together with carry-less multiplication for cryptographic and polynomial arithmetic workloads.

Instructions covered: AESENC, AESENCLAST, AESDEC, AESDECLAST, AESIMC, AESKEYGENASSIST, and PCLMULQDQ.

item.title: Encoding PADD/PSUB, PADDS/PSUBS, and PADDUS/PSUBUS
item.description:
Adding packed integer addition and subtraction across multiple lane widths, including signed and unsigned saturating forms for arithmetic that clamps instead of wrapping.

Instructions covered: PADDB/WDQ, PADDUSB/USW, PADDSB/SW, PSUBB/WD, PSUBUSB/USW, and PSUBSB/SW.

item.title: Encoding PMADD, PMULDQ/UDQ, PMULH, and PMULL
item.description:
Adding packed integer multiply instructions for low and high products, signed and unsigned widening multiplication, rounded high-word multiplication, and horizontal multiply-add operations.

Instructions covered: PMADDUBSW, PMADDWD, PMULDQ, PMULHRSW, PMULHUW, PMULHW, PMULLD, PMULLW, and PMULUDQ.

item.title: Encoding PAVG, PMAXS/U, PMINS/U, and PSIGN
item.description:
Adding packed integer average, signed and unsigned minimum/maximum, and sign-control instructions across legacy SSE and VEX encodings.

Instructions covered: PAVG, VPAVG, PMAXS, VPMAXS, PMAXU, VPMAXU, PMINS, VPMINS, PMINU, VPMINU, PSIGN, and VPSIGN.

item.title: Encoding PACKSS, PACKUS, PUNPCKL, and PUNPCKH
item.description:
Adding signed and unsigned packed narrowing with saturation, plus low- and high-half unpacking for interleaving packed integer lanes across multiple element widths.

Instructions covered: PACKSSDW/WB, PACKUSDW/WB, PUNPCKLBW/WD/DQ/QDQ, and PUNPCKHBW/WD/DQ/QDQ.

item.title: Encoding PSHUFB/D/LW/HW and PALIGNR
item.description:
Adding packed byte and doubleword shuffles, low- and high-word shuffles, and byte alignment across concatenated packed operands.

Instructions covered: PSHUFB/D, PSHUFLW, PSHUFHW, and PALIGNR.

item.title: Encoding PSLL, PSRA, PSRL, VPSLLV, VPSRAV, and VPSRLV
item.description:
Adding packed logical and arithmetic shifts with immediate, scalar-count, and per-lane variable-count forms across SSE, AVX, and AVX2 encodings.

Instructions covered: PSLL, PSRA, PSRL, VPSLLV, VPSRAV, and VPSRLV.

item.title: Encoding PMOVMSKB, PMOVSX, PMOVZX, PEXTR, and PINSR
item.description:
Adding packed sign and zero extension, byte-mask extraction, and packed element insertion and extraction between vector, register, and memory operands.

Instructions covered: PMOVMSKB, PMOVSX, PMOVZX, PEXTR, and PINSR.

item.title: Encoding PABS, PAND, PANDN, POR, PXOR, and PTEST
item.description:
Adding packed absolute value, bitwise logic, and packed test instructions across SSE, AVX, and AVX-512 forms.

Instructions covered: PAND, PANDN, POR, PXOR, PTEST, and PABSB/W/D/Q.

item.title: Encoding VPBLENDD, VPBROADCAST, VBROADCAST, VINSERT, and VEXTRACT
item.description:
Adding packed blend selection, scalar-to-vector broadcasts, and 128-bit lane insertion and extraction across AVX, AVX2, and AVX-512 encodings.

Instructions covered: VPBLENDD, VPBROADCASTB/W/D/Q, VBROADCASTBI32/F32/I64/F64/I128, VINSERTF128/I128, and VEXTRACTF128/I128.

item.title: Encoding VPERM2F128, VPERMW/D/Q, VPERMILPS, and VPERMPS/PD
item.description:
Note: Bad audio (popping) from 18:40 to 20:40 because Linux...

Adding immediate- and vector-controlled permutation instructions for rearranging 128-bit lanes and packed word, doubleword, quadword, and floating-point elements across AVX, AVX2, and AVX-512 forms.

Instructions covered: VPERM2F128, VPERMW/D/Q, VPERMILPS, and VPERMPS/PD.

item.title: Encoding VBROADCAST, VCVTPD2PH, VCVTPH2PD/PS/PSX, and VCVTPS2PH/PHX
item.description:
Adding floating-point broadcast instructions and packed conversions between half-, single-, and double-precision values, including newer EVEX opcode maps and extended conversion forms.

Instructions covered: VBROADCASTSS, VBROADCASTSD, VBROADCASTF128, VBROADCASTF32X2, VBROADCASTF32X4, VBROADCASTF32X8, VBROADCASTF64X2, VBROADCASTF64X4.

item.title: Encoding VFMADD, VFMSUB, VFNMADD, and VFNMSUB
item.description:
Adding fused multiply-add and multiply-subtract instructions, including negated variants, scalar and packed forms, and all 132/213/231 operand orderings across VEX and EVEX encodings.

Instructions covered: VFMADD132/213/231PS/PD/SS/SD, VFMSUB132/213/231PS/PD/SS/SD, VFNMADD132/213/231PS/PD/SS/SD, and VFNMSUB132/213/231PS/PD/SS/SD.

item.title: Encoding VGATHER, VSCATTER, VPGATHER, and VPSCATTER
item.description:
Adding floating-point and packed-integer gather and scatter instructions, together with VSIB addressing, vector index registers, high-16 EVEX indices, and no-base address encoding.

Instructions covered: VGATHERDPS/DPD, VGATHERQPS/QPD, VPGATHERDD/DQ/QD/QQ, VPSCATTERDD/DQ/QD/QQ, VSCATTERDPS/DPD, and VSCATTERQPS/QPD.

item.title: Encoding AVX-512 Mask Register Instructions
item.description:
Adding AVX-512 mask-register moves, arithmetic, logic, shifts, tests, and unpacking across byte, word, doubleword, and quadword element widths.

Instructions covered: KADDB/W/D/Q, KANDB/W/D/Q, KANDNB/W/D/Q, KMOVB/W/D/Q, KNOTB/W/D/Q, KORB/W/D/Q, KORTESTB/W/D/Q, KSHIFTLB/W/D/Q, KSHIFTRB/W/D/Q, KTESTB/W/D/Q, KUNPCKBW/WD/DQ, KXNORB/W/D/Q, and KXORB/W/D/Q.

item.title: Encoding VPCMP, VPMOV, and VPMASKMOV
item.description:
Adding AVX-512 packed integer comparisons that produce mask-register results, conversions between vector elements and mask registers, and AVX2 masked integer memory operations.

Instructions covered: VPCMPB/UB, VPCMPD/UD, VPCMPQ/UQ, VPCMPW/UW, VPMOVB2M/W2M/D2M/Q2M, VPMOVM2B/M2W/M2D/M2Q, and VPMASKMOVD/Q.

item.title: Encoding UNPCKL, UNPCKH, ROUND, LDMXCSR, and STMXCSR
item.description:
Adding low- and high-half floating-point unpacking, scalar and packed rounding, and MXCSR control-register loads and stores across legacy SSE and VEX encodings.

Instructions covered: UNPCKLPS/LPD, UNPCKHPS/HPD, ROUNDSS/SD, ROUNDPS/PD, LDMXCSR, and STMXCSR.

item.title: Encoding VPERM2I128, VPERMILPD, VZEROUPPER, and VZEROALL
item.description:
Adding 128-bit integer lane permutation, packed double-precision element permutation, and AVX state-transition instructions for clearing upper vector-register state.

Instructions covered: VPERM2I128, VPERMILPD, VZEROUPPER, and VZEROALL.

item.title: Encoding CMPXCHG8B/16B, CLD, STD, and ENDBR64
item.description:
Adding 8- and 16-byte atomic compare-exchange instructions, direction-flag control, and the ENDBR64 landing-pad instruction used by CET indirect branch tracking.

Instructions covered: CMPXCHG8B, CMPXCHG16B, CLD, STD, and ENDBR64.

item.title: Cleanup and Validation
item.description: Cleaning up some of the code in the encoder and adding tests to validate forms.

item.title: Improving Performance
item.description:
Code cleanup and performance improvements.

I start with a reference number of instructions per second using Odin and the benchmarks in its rexcode package. The numbers from that benchmark are purely used as a throughput target for my own encoder and are not in any way a language benchmark.

I take my encoder from ~26M insts/s to ~100M insts/s on the generic path, and up to ~180M insts/s on the cached instruction form path.

item.title: Recording Labels and Fixups
item.description: Before moving onto writing relocatable object files I need to track various offsets in the encoded bytes for things like labels and fixups.

item.title: Fixing an SAE Bug
item.description: I fix an SAE bug in the VCVTPS2PH instruction and do some final clean up.

item.title: ELF Relocatable Object File Types and Data Structures
item.description: I gather ELF data types and structures from the gABI and psABI spec PDFs in preparation for writing ELF relocatable object files.

item.title: Writing a Basic ELF Relocatable Object File
item.description: I start to output a basic ELF relocatable object file which can be given to an external linker, like ld, to create a basic executable binary.

item.title: Fixing Destructive Fixups
item.description: Before I can reliably create ELF relocations I need to fix my encoder fixups, which are destroying important data required for encoding the correct instruction bytes.

item.title: Adding Symbols to ELF Objects
item.description: I implement the basics of adding symbols to an ELF relocatable object file, which to start with allows me to link using ld without any warnings.

item.title: Adding Relocations to ELF Objects
item.description: I add relocation sections and entries to ELF relocatable object files, then connect encoder fixups to ELF symbols and relocations for external function calls and RIP-relative data references.

item.title: Changes to Support .bss and Cleanup
item.description: I add support for .bss sections by separating their logical in-memory size from file data, then clean up repeated writes and make relocation-section lookup more reliable.

item.title: Fixing EVEX and Memory Encoding Edge Cases
item.description: I fix an incorrect LOCK prefix byte and displacement-selection bugs affecting byte-width and EVEX no-base memory operands, then update accumulator instruction forms to select shorter sign-extended immediate encodings.

item.title: COFF Object File Types and Data Structures
item.description: I gather COFF data structures and constants from Microsoft's PE format documentation in preparation for writing Windows object files for link.exe. I cover file and section headers, AMD64 relocations, symbols, and the string table, including differences from ELF and how COFF handles long names and relocation addends.

item.title: Writing a Minimal COFF Object File
item.description: I implement a minimal COFF object file writer with file and section headers, aligned section data, a basic symbol table, and an empty string table. I inspect the output with dumpbin, link a small program with link.exe that returns 123, then correct the handling of .bss section sizes.

item.title: Adding Relocations to COFF Objects
item.description: I connect encoder fixups to COFF relocations, write relocation tables after each section's data, and clear fixup bytes to avoid unwanted implicit addends. I inspect the output with dumpbin, then link against libcmt and run a program that calls printf and returns 123.

item.title: Long COFF Symbol and Section Names and Relocation Overflow
item.description: I add string-table support for COFF symbol and section names longer than eight bytes, then implement relocation overflow handling with a section flag and a dummy relocation record. I inspect the long names with dumpbin, link and run a program that calls GetStdHandle and printf and returns 123, then fix the overflow flag output and relocation count.

item.title: Writing a Scanner for an Assembler
item.description: I design the initial syntax for the assembler, then implement a scanner with source files, token kinds, line and column lookup, whitespace and comment handling, and support for strings, identifiers, keywords, punctuation, and number literals.

item.title: Tracking Trivia Tokens in the Scanner
item.description: I add support for tracking comment trivia in the assembler's scanner, including leading comments, inline comments, and comments before the end-of-file token. I store trivia separately from significant tokens and associate it with source offsets so it can later be used for formatting and compact parser tests.

item.title: Fixing Scanner Bugs
item.description: I clean up the scanner API, then add regression tests and fix bugs in ellipsis detection, comment trivia at the end of a file, and unterminated string literals. I correct how EOF handles leading and inline trivia, prevent the scanner cursor from moving beyond the source, and return invalid tokens for strings that reach a newline or EOF without a closing delimiter.

item.title: Comment-Driven Parser Test Setup
item.description: I set up parser tests that put expected AST output as s-expression comments beside assembler source. I build a test runner that scans source files, matches leading comment trivia to AST nodes, and compares the expected text with formatted nodes. I then add initial AST types and traversal, implement a simple parser for const declarations and integer expressions, and get the first two tests passing.

item.title: Recursive Descent Expression Parsing
item.description: I add recursive descent parsing for assembler expressions, using separate expression, term, and factor parsers to handle operator precedence, left associativity, and parentheses. I extend the AST with number, group, and binary nodes, then refine parser recovery and the comment-driven test runner to handle newlines, file nodes, and overlapping source offsets.

item.title: Parsing Section and Object Declarations
item.description: I add parsing for section and object declarations, including optional section alignment, array types with explicit or inferred lengths, and list initialisers. I extend the AST, its formatting, and traversal, add token-consumption checks and parser errors with line and column numbers, then implement string literals with newline escapes and fix multiline list parsing.

item.title: Parsing Import and Function Declarations
item.description: I add parsing for import and function declarations, including namespaced attributes, instruction blocks, labels, alignment statements, and memory operands. I extend the AST, its traversal, and s-expression formatting, handle typed nil pointers during traversal, then fix duplicate newline consumption and add optional width suffixes to identifiers, numbers, and memory expressions.

item.title: Fixing Scanner and Parser Bugs
item.description: I work through scanner and parser bugs before moving on to semantic analysis. I switch source storage to a byte slice, fix EOF handling and empty-file trivia, and support escaped quotes and backslashes in strings. I then improve parser recovery with synthetic tokens and configurable stopping points, extract a helper for width suffixes, require newlines after declarations, and fix an infinite loop when parsing invalid function attributes.

item.title: Unary Prefix Operators and Object Align and Attributes
item.description: I finish the remaining parser features before moving on to semantic analysis. I add optional alignment and attributes to object declarations, allow const declarations inside function bodies, and extend the expression parser with unary plus and minus. I separate primary expressions, postfix width suffixes and unary prefix operators, and update the AST traversal and printing.

item.title: Restructuring Assembler Packages
item.description: I consolidate the scanner, parser, tokens and AST into a single assembler package before moving on to semantic analysis. I resolve name collisions, rename AST helpers and token types, and update the tests and imports. Along the way, I fix object spans to include alignment and attributes, organise parser test data into its own directory, and add a check that parser tests actually run.

item.title: Symbol Resolution and Constant Expression Evaluation
item.description: I start the assembler's semantic analysis with a resolver that maps AST nodes to symbols. I add symbol and type representations, scopes with parent lookup, and annotated AST output for resolver tests. I then implement constant expression evaluation for integer literals, identifiers and binary arithmetic, cache values on symbols, and fix symbol storage and identifier resolution while keeping undefined-symbol errors in the resolution pass.

item.title: Section and Object Symbol Resolution
item.description: I extend the assembler's resolver to handle section and object declarations. I add section attributes and constant alignment evaluation, associate objects with their section and type, and introduce an architecture scope for built-in symbols that cannot be shadowed. I update the annotated AST output, check that objects are declared within a section, and switch source storage back to a string to avoid repeated substring conversions.

item.title: Resolving Imports, Functions, and Aligns
item.description: I extend the assembler's resolver to handle object alignment, standalone align statements, imports and function bodies. I cache evaluated alignments and add parser support for top-level align statements. I then mark imported function and object symbols, resolve instruction arguments within block scopes, and add built-in register symbols before updating the annotated AST output and resolver tests.

item.title: Resolving Forward References for Labels, Functions, and Objects
item.description: I add a declaration pass to the assembler's resolver so labels, functions and objects can be referenced before they appear in the source. I fix constant expression evaluation to run before declaring the constant's symbol, pre-declare symbols in global and block scopes, and debug a recursive call and missing AST symbol associations. I then resolve names inside memory and sized operands and add support for labels attached to align statements.

item.title: Resolving Array Types and Inferring Lengths
item.description: I extend the assembler's resolver to handle array types, evaluate explicit lengths and infer lengths from simple initialiser lists. I separate type resolution from symbol lookup, add size and alignment helpers, and update the annotated AST output for nested arrays while debugging a recursive size calculation. I also support forward references to imported symbols, add predefined data section mappings, evaluate grouped expressions and unary plus and minus, and reset the resolver's state between runs. Nested inferred array lengths and further validation are left for later.

item.title: Resolving Nested Array Types
item.description: I extend the assembler's type resolver to support nested arrays with explicit and inferred lengths, using the largest initialiser at each dimension to infer its length. I pass initialisers through recursive type resolution, support direct string initialisers and count their UTF-8 bytes, then fix the parser to accept nested initialiser lists. I test nested strings and different element sizes, reject strings used with non-i8 arrays and initialisers that exceed explicit lengths, and turn constant division by zero into a resolver error instead of a Go panic.

item.title: Building the First Bootstrap Compiler
item.description:
Preparing New Imports

In the previous post I set up a working executable that could call the GetProcessVersion function which was imported from kernel32.dll.

This is a good start because it means I've got access to everything I need to start writing the initial bootstrap compiler. So, in this post I'll get a basic initial bootstrap compiler up and running that can compile a source file that contains binary in the form of hex ASCII characters, and comments, which I can use to annotate my machine code to make it easier to follow.

item.title: Preparing a PE32+ Executable by Hand
item.description:
Introduction

I wanted document the process of bootstrapping a simple compiler directly from x86-64 machine code, so that's what I'm going to do in these posts.

The plan is to implement the initial, very simple compiler using machine code, which I'll then use to implement the next compiler, and so on and so forth (a.k.a. "bootstrapping").

I need some way to create binary files, so I'll be using the HxD hex editor to complete this initial stage of the project.
